data.content_ref: inline:The audit-ritual problem (§11.3) asks whether the 'adjudication-ritual flags sustained' were properly sustained. SRC_001's argument for §11.3 flags attacks the oracle's methodology by claiming it relies on SRC_005 as ground truth without independent verification. However, an audit of adjudication flags examines whether the flagging process followed proper adjudication procedures (as stated in the problem context: 'adjudication-ritual flags sustained (§11.3)'). The argument does not identify any procedural irregularity in the adjudication process itself—no misapplied threshold, no procedural violation, no improper flag elevation or suppression. The argument instead substitutes an epistemological critique of oracle design (whether the ground-truth source is verifiable) for the actual audit question (whether the adjudication flags were properly sustained). By §11.3's own scope, adjudication-ritual flags are sustained through a defined process; an argument that the ground-truth artifact might be wrong does not establish that the flag-sustaining process was defective. The claim that dissenting critics face 'systematic asymmetry' is asserted without evidence of any actual misadjudicated flag, making it a speculative design objection rather than a demonstrated audit failure.
